chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: The stoop band: kazoo, cheese-box drum and Ervin Butler
summary: Danny drew crowds with ukulele, kazoo and a cheese-box drum, until Ervin Butler offered to take them out to earn money.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So we're sitting on my steps. Now, Joe Francis Ely(?) is on the corner. He's a presser's son. He gets the kazoo, he comes around. Then with the ukelele, I'm drawing a crowd. I've become a little celebrity with the ukelele.
Joe comes with the kazoo. Russell, another friend of ours, he's got the drum. He gets the top of a cheese-box and had a little drum. And we're sitting on my steps.
Now, every evening there's a concert. And the people would stop, because we were beginning to sound good. "Little Liza Jane"...

We've got a beat. We've definitely got the beat. Because you would learn that beat from the street parades, that funky beat, the snappin' the fingers. The second... All the little cats on the street are second-lining, you know, with "The Saints..."

So we've got this group. So here comes Ervin Butler. Ervin Butler's a hustler in town, a young cat, a roughneck, fight anybody anywhere, any time, and go anywhere -- because they had them gang wars with youngsters. Well, Ervin Butler would go anywhere. He'd go to Cherokee, you know, and the various streets where you have them gangs. You know, like on the South Side of Chicago, man, they have certain neighborhoods that you don't go if you're out of bounds. Well, Ervin Butler would go everywhere.
He sees us. He sits there and listens. And he says, "Man, you'all got a gold mine here, man. We could make some
money with this." I said, "How?" He said, "Well, come on with me, and I'll take you to the balls(?) on Saturday, and we'll make us some money."
